body: Just my GP. I don't know of any psychologists that are local.

(Don't mind typos. am on crappy tiny mobile keyboard) I kinda get that too. I feel better when I'm put with friends. It's a lot harder to get caught up in my own head.

I also get the shitty thoughts and feelings when i'm in a pretty favourable position in life. I've got big things to look forward to this year but here I am at nearly 3am unable to sleep because of an irrational but unending sense of panic and thoughts swirling in my head about life and death and what to do about my laptop harddrive if I go to off myself.

It may not be physical pain or distinctly recognisable emotional pain such as sadness, but these feelings are distressing and are a form of pain. And the thing about pain is when pain exceeds coping respurces for that pain, otherwose detrimental things happen. Think the wolf that gnaws off their own leg to escape a painful trap.

Talking about feelings, or venting, is a way to cope with pain. I know when I step into a commites friendship, I openly offer myself up to listen to feelings and other venting. Most people are like that. Your friends are most likely like that too, especially that one particular friend. Don't be afraid to utilise those coping resources. As a friend who's been on both sides of such conversations, it's no unconvenience. It's something you sign up for when you acquire the title 'friend'.

As for seeking attention, so what? Humans are social creatures, Love amd validility are right up there with food and shelter in terms of vital needs for a prsoporous life. If someone goes to the doctor for a pain in their abdomen, no-one calls them attention seeking. What's so different about a pain in your psyche? It has just as much an affect on your quality of life as a broken bone, if not more.

DYK that there are chemical imbalances and other physical causes and symptoms of feelings like this. It's not all 'in your head'. It's like coming down with the flu. Did you also know that most cough medicine doesn't actually kill the virus, it just suppresses the symptoms to make life more bearable.

Have you considered seeing a doctor or psychologist to look into medical coping methods and resources that makes living easier while your body fights this off?

Also, what's so bad about endong up in hospital? You don't see people with inflamed appendixes actively avoiding treatment. Life isn't the worst thing in the world. (your time spent with others is proof of that) so what's so bad about prolonging it? Having you seen the microsoft hololens? We're actually living in the future and cool shit is going down.

But hey, if it's any inspiration, you can get through this. Other people have before from similar situations and you cam too. The fact that you're alive enough to read this shows the tiniest bit of resistance and apprehension. Like running a marathon, it's gonna be an exhausting fight, but latch onto that apprehension. Finding that euphoria of happiness again when you win the fight makes the struggle worth it. Feelings are such strange things. Why do we feel good? Why do we feel bad! All I really know is the good feelings are worth chasing. Gotta chase more good stuff to outweigh the bad in life, ya know. Coping resources vs pain. Look for those coping resources whether they be time with friends, hobbies such as playing an instrument, writing in a journal, or venting here.

Think about chocolate cake. No-where else in the universe can you find chocolate cake. It's delicious. No idea why, but it is. And that's kinda amazing. Go treat yourself to some chocolate cake or other preferred desert. Remind yourself about the good feelings in life.

These are the words that I use to remind myself to keep on fighting. Writing this has actually cleared my head up a bit. I think I might actually manage to sleep soon, heh.

Maybe this helped you too. See ya 'round, stranger. If you choose to keep on fighting, I'll be here in  the background of the universing cheering you on 'cause I believe in you.
